name: WA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rick Larsen running with a large fundraising edge ($2.0M raised, $652K on hand)
Challenger Edwin Feller shows no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Larsen near certain (97%)
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Larsen: a D+12 district, incumbency, and a dominant money advantage against a challenger with no visible financial backing. Markets agree, pricing his win at 97%, so the race stays Safe Democratic with no evidence warranting a shift.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Larsen showing a closer-than-expected race would be the first sign of movement, but none is currently present.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Larsen, a long-serving Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northwestern Washington district that leans Democratic by about twelve points. He enters the general election with roughly two million dollars raised and a large cash advantage, while Republican Edwin Feller has reported minimal fundraising and no meaningful outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and money.

Prediction markets give Larsen about a 97 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's lean and his incumbency. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific sign of vulnerability.
